web_evidence.title: A Legacy of Spies — Penguin Books sample
web_evidence.note: The authorized 29-page Penguin sample sustains Peter Guillam’s participating “I/my” narration across the opening chapters. Its temporary “you” passage is a self-projected reconstruction within that first-person account.

web_evidence.title: A Legacy of Spies by John le Carré
web_evidence.note: The official publisher description identifies Peter Guillam as the book’s narrator and describes the past and present as parts of one interwoven plot.

web_evidence.title: A Legacy of Spies review – a final turn from Smiley’s Circus?
web_evidence.note: The Observer review explicitly says the novel is narrated by retired Circus officer Peter Guillam and notes that he reviews case documents during his account.

web_evidence.title: A Legacy of Spies by John le Carré - review
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly calls the novel first person, with Guillam writing in the present and recalling events fifty years earlier; it also explains that contemporaneous reports and documents are incorporated verbatim.

person_note: The controlling narrator is retired spy Peter Guillam, who participates in both the present inquiry and the remembered Windfall events and narrates them as “I.” Numerous event quotes independently expose that voice, including the programmatic opening q02332. The novel incorporates dialogue, transcripts, letters, reports, and third-person case-file passages; these are subordinate documents or locally unmarked material, not sustained changes in base narrator. Guillam’s extended use of “you” in q02314 is a self-projected reconstruction anchored by “me/I,” not second-person control. The quote evidence, authorized publisher sample, official publisher identification, and explicit whole-book reviews agree, with no credible structural conflict.
